title: Count Valid Prefixes
summary: Given a binary string, count the number of prefixes that can be rearranged to form an alternating string where no two adjacent characters are the same.
statement: Given a binary string, count the number of prefixes that can be rearranged to form an alternating string where no two adjacent characters are the same.
constraints: A prefix is valid when its characters can be rearranged into a binary alternating string.
That is possible exactly when its zero and one counts differ by at most one.
Return the number of nonempty valid prefixes.
hints: Maintain ones minus zeros for the growing prefix.
A rearranged alternating string exists exactly when the absolute balance is at most one.
Update once per character and count qualifying states.
Only counts matter because rearrangement can place the majority symbol at both ends when needed.
editorial: Only counts matter because rearrangement can place the majority symbol at both ends when needed.

tests.explanation: Prefixes of lengths one, three, and five have balanced-enough counts, giving three.
Every prefix has zero/one counts differing by at most one.
